Blue Ash man who placed hidden cameras in minor victims’ home sentenced to more than 16 years in prison for sexual exploitation of a child
item.description: CINCINNATI – A Blue Ash man who, for years, entered a private residence without permission to install and maintain hidden cameras in the bedrooms of two minors was sentenced in federal court here today to 200 months in prison.

item.title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 93 Border-Related Cases This Week
item.description: SAN DIEGO – Federal prosecutors in the Southern District of California filed 93 border-related cases this week, including charges of bringing in aliens for financial gain, reentering the U.S. after deportation, and importation of controlled substances. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California is the fourth-busiest federal district, largely due to a high volume of border-related crimes. This district, encompassing San Diego and Imperial counties, shares a 140-mile border with Mexico. It includes the San Ysidro Port of Entry, the world’s busiest land border crossing, connecting San Diego (America’s eighth largest city) and Tijuana (Mexico’s second largest city).

item.title: Maryland Brothers Sentenced for Tax Evasion
item.description: Baltimore, Maryland – A federal judge handed down prison terms to Maryland twin brothers, today, in connection with tax-evasion crimes. Judge Deborah K. Chasanow sentenced Dennis March, 55, and Greg March, 55, both of Berlin, to six months in prison each, followed by three years of supervised release — with a special condition of 12 months of home detention as part of their supervised-release term — for tax evasion. Judge Chasanow also ordered the March brothers to each pay restitution of nearly $1.8 million.

item.title: Justice Department Awards Jacksonville More Than $73M to Combat Violent Crime and Restore Law and Order Through Model Cities Initiative
item.description: Today, the Justice Department awarded Jacksonville, Florida, more than $73 Million through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a flagship effort to reduce violent crime, restore law and order, and strengthen public safety in communities across the country.

item.title: Folsom man sentenced to 15 years in prison for sexual exploitation of a child
item.description: William James Fitzgerald, 26, of Folsom, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Dena Coggins to 15 years in prison to be followed by 10 years of supervised release for sexual exploitation of a child.

item.title: Downtown Seattle drug dealer sentenced to five years in prison for having a gun while dealing crack cocaine
item.description: Seattle – A 24-year-old Seattle man was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Seattle to 5 years in prison for dealing cocaine while armed with a 9mm polymer gun with an extended magazine, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd.

item.title: Omaha Man Sentenced to 50 Years for Production and Possession of Child Pornography
item.description: Justin A. Dueling, 42, of Omaha, Nebraska, was sentenced on November 4, 2026, in federal court in Omaha, for production of child pornography and possession of child pornography.

item.title: Lincoln Man Sentenced to 70 Months for Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm
item.description: Corey Schneider, 51, of Lincoln, Nebraska, was sentenced on November 4, 2026, in federal court in Lincoln for possession of a firearm by a prohibited person.

item.title: Omaha Man Sentenced to 18 Years in Prison for Conspiring to Distribute Methamphetamine
item.description: Keith Pumala, 67, of Omaha, Nebraska, was sentenced on November 5, 2026, in federal court in Omaha for conspiracy to distribute and possess with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of a mixture of methamphetamine.

item.title: Two Columbia Men Charged with Possession of Ammunition After Saturday Morning Shooting
item.description: Detravion Latrell Coats, 21, and Treyvale Damarcus Cain-Raybon, 21, both of Columbia, Mo., appeared in federal court today on complaints alleging they possessed ammunition after a prior felony conviction.

item.title: Políticos, Empresarios Y Narcotraficantes Ecuatorianos Detenidos Por Delitos De Importación De Estupefacientes Y Armas
item.description: El fiscal federal del Distrito Sur de Nueva York, Jamie McDonald, y el administrador de la Agencia Antidroga de Estados Unidos (DEA), Terrance Cole, han anunciado hoy la revelación de los cargos y la detención de cinco ciudadanos ecuatorianos que conspiraron para importar grandes cantidades de cocaína a los Estados Unidos durante más de una década.

item.title: Peoria Man Sentenced to 42 Months in Prison for Possession of a Firearm
item.description: A Peoria, Illinois, man, Quincy Jones, 36, was sentenced on November 4, 2026, to 42 months of imprisonment, to be followed by three years of supervised release, on each of two counts of possessing a firearm as a felon.

item.title: Boise Man Sentenced To 15 Years in Federal Prison for Producing Child Sexual Abuse Material
item.description: Gregory Conan Williams, 41, of Boise, Idaho, was sentenced to 188 months in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor child, U.S. Attorney John C. Shirts announced today.
